newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia forecasts cement oversupply in 1997/98. [CORRECTED 08:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Indonesia forecasts cement oversupply in 1997/98. [CORRECTED 08:00 GMT]

text.p: Indonesia's ministry of industry and trade said on Monday the country would begin facing an oversupply of cement in 1997 and 1998 (corrects year) due to increases in production.
The ministry said in a report during a parliament hearing that cement demand would rise to 33.04 million tonnes in 1998 from 29.5 million tonnes in 1997.
It said the rises was forecast to be exceeded by estimated installed capacity of 46.87 million tonnes and production of 38.95 million tonnes in 1998.
Installed capacity and production were forecast to rise to 34.22 million tonnes and 30.93 million tonnes, respectively, in 1997, the ministry said.
It said cement had to be imported in 1995 and 1996 due to shortages in domestic production capacity.
The report said demand was forecast to hit 26.34 million tonnes in 1996, compared with domestic production of 25.86 million tonnes.
It said cement production in 1995 was 23.13 million tonnes against overall demand of 24.04 million tonnes.
